newsitem.title: USA: Nebraska fed cattle trade slow after record sales.
newsitem.headline: Nebraska fed cattle trade slow after record sales.

text.p: Nebraska feedlot cattle markets were slow following Wednesday's record large daily sales, market sources and USDA said.
About 600 head of slaughter steers and heifers sold Thursday at $110.00 to $111.00 per cwt on a dressed basis, steady with Wednesday, they said.

Wednesday's sale of 94,400 head was the largest single day trade of fed cattle in Nebraska, topping the 92,072 sold August 16, 1996, USDA reported. The record sales left most showlists depleted, with only a minimal number of steers and heifers left, sources said.
